method total_match(lst1: seq<string>, lst2: seq<string>) returns (result: seq<string>)
    requires |lst1| >= 0 && |lst2| >= 0 // both lists can be of any non-negative length
    ensures (|lst1| == 0 && |lst2| == 0 ==> result == []) // if both lists are empty, return empty list
    ensures (|lst1| > 0 && |lst2| == 0 ==> result == lst1) // if lst2 is empty, return lst1
    ensures (|lst1| == 0 && |lst2| > 0 ==> result == lst2) // if lst1 is empty, return lst2
    ensures (sumChars(lst1) < sumChars(lst2) ==> result == lst1) // if total chars in lst1 < lst2, return lst1
    ensures (sumChars(lst1) > sumChars(lst2) ==> result == lst2) // if total chars in lst1 > lst2, return lst2
    ensures (sumChars(lst1) == sumChars(lst2) ==> result == lst1) // if total chars are equal, return lst1

method sumChars(lst: seq<string>) returns (total: int)
    requires |lst| >= 0
    ensures total >= 0 // total number of characters is non-negative
    ensures total == |lst| * 0 + (forall i: int :: 0 <= i < |lst| ==> |lst[i]|) // total is the sum of the lengths of the strings in lst
```
